absent: Detailed behavior of memory_failure and soft_offline_page beyond queue dispatch is not shown.
Revocation and signalling performed by unmap_and_kill and the common add helper is not shown.
Filesystem-specific error removal, buffer release and invalidation semantics is not shown.
Enablement, filtering criteria and lifecycle of the optional poison filter hook is not shown.
Payload and consumers of resource tracing and the meaning of its member selector is not shown.
Command-line spelling for the randomization boot option and compatibility-brk default interaction is not fully shown.
Structure and translation contract of pfn_address_space beyond its interval node and hook presence check is not shown.

findings.text: PFN space registry offers insertion and removal of interval descriptors. Insertion requires a translation hook and rejects overlaps, while removal drops the range when present. A dedicated mutex guards the shared cached index across both operations.

DAX failure service provides extent revocation with mandatory termination semantics. Its contract covers poison marking except during pre-removal revocation, collection of affected file-backed mappings, and busy reporting when an entry cannot be secured, with each processed offset left unlocked.

Deferred failure submission accepts a frame number with flags for processor-local queuing and asynchronous handling. Successful insertion schedules local work, with enqueue and scheduling performed under interrupt-safe per-processor serialization.
Taken-off markers manage a magic tag in page private storage. The set operation stores the tag, while the clear operation resets storage only for pages that remain poisoned.

Raw poison query distinguishes ordinary and huge cases. Non-huge poisoned pages report true, unreliable huge tracking reports true for all subpages, and otherwise exact subpage membership is determined by scanning a folio raw list under the global failure mutex.

Address-space globals expose a highest mappable frame watermark, a per-mm resource reporter forwarding a member selector to tracing, and a randomization switch defaulting to enabled with a kernel control for adjustment.
Termination candidate record holds a list linkage, a task reference, a fault address, and a size encoded as a shift. Instances are collected for later revocation and signalling.
Poison walk context combines a termination candidate with a target frame number and a flag word. Discovery callbacks populate the embedded candidate upon locating the target.
Error dispatch descriptor contains a flag mask with expected value, a page-type tag, and a handler callback. Its contract obliges the handler to release the page lock before returning a disposition.
Raw poison node joins a lock-free list linkage with a page pointer, enabling a folio to enumerate precisely which subpages carry raw poison.

Deferred queue element carries a frame number with flags. Per-processor state pairs a small fixed-capacity queue of elements with interrupt-safe serialization and a work item used for asynchronous drain.

Per-node failure statistics appear as read-only attributes under a dedicated memory failure group. Five counters cover total, ignored, failed, delayed and recovered outcomes, each sourced from node-local statistics.

Failure tunables default to recovery enabled and soft offline enabled, with early kill and panic on unrecoverable disabled. The poisoned-page count starts at zero and the global failure indicator starts false, all held as mostly-read data.

Error classification matches page flags against mask and expected values in table order, addressing huge pages first, then swap-cache, mlocked, unevictable and LRU pairs with dirty versus clean distinction, ending in an unconditional unknown entry that must remain last.

Poison matching accepts both present mappings and encoded poison entries, aligns the target to the mapping granularity, and derives the poisoned address from the mapping base plus the intra-compound offset. Transparent huge handling may be compiled out, in which case its check reports no match.
An optional hardware-poison filter hook is held as an RCU-protected pointer that starts absent and resides in mostly-read storage.
LRU detachment on poisoned folios clears reclaim-related flags, releases memory accounting, and drops the isolation reference upon success, signalling an I/O error when isolation fails.

Reference surplus assessment discounts the expected handling reference and additionally discounts the folio page count when extra pins are anticipated. Any remainder is logged with its page-type label and treated as a surplus.

DAX collection derives a file-backed address for each candidate mapping and records it for termination. Pre-removal revocation considers all tasks, while normal operation restricts attention through a per-task selection predicate, keeping only mappings whose address space matches.
Global failure mutex protects traversal of the folio raw poison list during huge-page membership queries against concurrent modification.
PFN interval mutex serializes overlap lookup, insertion and removal on the shared cached interval tree.
Per-processor failure serialization guards queue insertion, removal and the scheduling decision, with lock, queue storage and work item initialized for every possible processor during boot.

DAX task enumeration holds mapping read serialization together with RCU protection while inspecting tasks and reverse mappings. Table inspection holds page-table or huge-page serialization while examining entries within a walk.

Page recovery dispatches by flag pattern to a dedicated handler yielding ignored, failed, delayed or recovered. Clean page-cache and clean swap-cache outcomes lean toward recovered, dirty swap-cache toward delayed, and unknown state toward ignored, with surplus references forcing failure.

Deferred drain services the full backlog of queued entries, directing soft-offline types to soft handling and remaining entries to synchronous failure handling. Work is scheduled only when insertion succeeds.

Table search covers transparent huge mappings and small-page ranges, yielding at most one poison location per walk. Huge entries use dedicated examination, and PFN-map areas remain visitable through a permissive test.
Boot setup registers failure controls under one namespace and randomization control under another, prepares per-processor failure queues, and offers a boot option that forces randomization off.
Poison discovery installs a read-locked walk set with a table-range callback, a huge-page callback that is null when huge support is absent, and a permissive test callback.

Queue overflow discards the newest report with an error, so bursts beyond capacity lose work. Surplus page references downgrade otherwise successful handling to failure, and unknown states are logged and counted as ignored.

File-backed recovery prefers a filesystem error-removal hook with buffer release, falling back to invalidation when unsupported. Dirty file data is surfaced as a mapping error for writers, and the fragments record an open question about filesystem locking during truncation.

Queue sizing uses order four for sixteen entries. Page acquisition allows at most three retries. Huge dispositions use six consecutive small codes for freed, in-use, non-huge, folio pre-poisoned, page pre-poisoned and busy-retry conditions.

Failure controls appear under vm as four bounded zero-to-one integers, owner-writable and group-readable. Their names are memory_failure_early_kill and memory_failure_recovery and enable_soft_offline and panic_on_unrecoverable_memory_failure. Sysfs provides five read-only counters under memory_failure, with Unpoison and Soft offline log prefixes.

Randomization control randomize_va_space appears under kernel as an owner-writable integer. Outcome vocabulary uses Ignored and Failed and Delayed and Recovered. Page-type vocabulary distinguishes kernel, huge, swap-cache, mlocked, unevictable, LRU, buddy, DAX, poisoned and unknown cases.
